statement: On a straight road, Ana lives 10 km from Bo, and Bo 4 km from Cy. Dee lives halfway between Ana and Cy, closer to Ana than to Bo. How far is Dee from Bo?

choices.misconception: I put Cy on the far side of Bo, 14 km from Ana, so Dee was at 7 km, 3 km from Bo, and I did not check that Dee must be closer to Ana.
I put Dee halfway between Ana and Bo instead of halfway between Ana and Cy.
I found the distance from Ana to Cy, 6 km, and gave that as the answer.
I put Dee halfway between Bo and Cy instead of halfway between Ana and Cy.

hints: Put Ana at 0 and Bo at 10 on a number line.
Cy is 4 km from Bo, so there are two places Cy could be. For each one, find the point halfway between Ana and Cy, then use the last clue.
Cy is at 6 or at 14, so Dee is at 3 or at 7. Which of these is closer to Ana than to Bo?

solutions.reliable: Put Ana at 0 and Bo at 10 (the picture can always be flipped). Cy is 4 km from Bo, so Cy is at 6 or at 14. Halfway between Ana and Cy is then 3 or 7. At 7, Dee would be 7 km from Ana but only 3 km from Bo, so she would be closer to Bo, and that case fails. At 3, Dee is 3 km from Ana and 7 km from Bo, as the clue needs. So Bo and Dee live $10 - 3 = 7$ km apart. The transferable idea: when a distance could go either way, draw both cases and let the last clue choose.
solutions.elegant: Dee is closer to Ana than to Bo, so she is less than 5 km from Ana, on the half of the road nearer Ana. Cy is twice as far from Ana as Dee is, so Cy is less than 10 km from Ana: Cy must be at 6, between Ana and Bo, not at 14. Then Dee is at 3, which is $10 - 3 = 7$ km from Bo.

whyOnTest: Betweenness on a line: a distance allows two positions, and a halfway point plus a final clue rules out every case but one.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
